title: Review of c38's coevbits robustness: replicated on fresh seed 7 for two arms. Late new predator genotypes nb20 w8 109 vs 2 and nb24 w12 23 vs 3 against the neutral twins, prey near neutral, and both arms show the prey-led time-shift dip
summary: New seed 7, T=200000, with c38's own drivebits.py, twincal.py (BWF 0.1, q99.9) and the robust finding's timeshift2.py (W and NB set per arm). Arms: nb=20, w=8 and nb=24, w=12, each with its constant-capture twin (p0 0.115361 and 0.244316, the runs' realised means). Late significant new predator genotypes, real vs twin: w8 109 vs 2 (c38: 91-111 vs 1-2); nb24 w12 23 vs 3 (c38: 8-28 vs 2-4). Prey: 32 vs 27 and 39 vs 29, near neutral. Time-shift capture at lags -40k/-8k/0/+8k/+40k: w8 0.268/0.236/0.195/0.156/0.236; nb24 w12 0.368/0.346/0.296/0.251/0.292. The +8k over -40k ratio is 0.58 and 0.68 (c38's minima 0.54 and 0.59). The w=12, nb=20 arm was not re-run. Note: c38's earlier timeshift.py hard-codes w=10 unless W is set, so timeshift2.py with the run's W is needed for these arms (at w=10 I get 0.41/0.33/0.28 for w8).

observations.finding: robust_s7.txt: pred late q99.9 w8 109 vs 2, nb24 w12 23 vs 3; ts2_s7.txt: dip after lag 0 in both arms

controls_run.finding: constant-capture twins b8N and n24w12N on seed 7

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm; two of the three arms. The twin removes all selection, so beating it shows adaptive turnover, not open-endedness.
